items.title: Kering holds steady, but Gucci remains a cause for concern
items.summary: Kering's Q3 revenue was essentially flat at EUR 3.35 billion group-wide, with like-for-like revenue down 1% and nine-month revenue down 2% to EUR 10.6 billion, but the article frames Gucci's ongoing sales decline as the group's persistent drag even as Saint Laurent and Bottega Veneta outperform. CEO Luca de Meo continues cutting the retail network to restore profitability.

items.title: Kering-Aktie: Gucci enttäuscht erneut (Gucci disappoints again)
items.summary: German financial wire reports Kering shares fell roughly 11% to a new yearly low near EUR 189 after Gucci's comparable sales decline deepened to 6% (EUR 1.29bn Q3 revenue) from a 2% decline in Q2. CFO Armelle Poulou would not confirm a return to profitability by year-end, which the market read as a warning sign; UBS cut its price target from EUR 285 to EUR 224 and trimmed 2027 earnings estimates by 14%.

items.title: Citi cuts Kering target, signaling end of Gucci's improvement
items.summary: Citi cut its Kering price target from EUR 243 to EUR 201 (neutral rating), calling Q3 'a real setback' for Gucci after several quarters of gradual improvement, driven by a sharp decline in directly-operated store sales. The note says Saint Laurent, Bottega Veneta, eyewear and jewelry growth is normalizing and no longer enough to offset Gucci's shortfall, and flags continued weak store traffic and a gloomy macro backdrop for luxury.

items.title: Kering dévisse après un recul des ventes de Gucci, rude hiver en vue pour le luxe
items.summary: French financial press reports Gucci Q3 sales fell 6% to EUR 1.29bn, dragging group comparable revenue down 1%. Bernstein noted Kering's outlook no longer mentions a return-to-growth ambition; TD Cowen said a Q4 return to growth 'appears unlikely.' Even Hermes showed its weakest quarterly growth since 2020, framing a tough winter across European luxury.

items.title: Forum members review the 'vulgar' Gucci Spring 2027 collection from Demna
items.summary: theFashionSpot forum thread reacting to Demna's fifth Gucci collection (Milan, 'The Store Show') skewed sharply negative. One member called it 'pure vulgarity,' another wrote 'what a pile of nothingness,' and one predicted it would be 'his final season.' No positive member comments were captured in this roundup, illustrating a vocal critical fan-community segment distinct from more measured trade-press takes.

items.title: Social reaction to Demna's Gucci 'The Store Show' divides X users
items.summary: Posts around Demna's Milan presentation split between celebrity-power coverage (Shawn Mendes, Bianca Jagger, Cardi B front row) and mocking commentary comparing models' stylized walk to video-game NPCs; Kate Moss's closing thong-dress look drew both admiring and critical replies. Overall thread sentiment was polarized rather than uniformly promotional.

items.title: Gucci lowers prices: Luca de Meo's strategy
items.summary: Report on de Meo's three-phase turnaround (structural reset by end-2026, rebuild phase to 2028, leadership ambition by 2030) in which he admitted the brand had 'pushed prices a little too high' and is now targeting an average retail band of EUR 2,000-3,000, with roughly a 20% cut on carry-over items, alongside a EUR 1 billion reduction in unsold inventory and continued store-network shrinkage.

items.title: Italian consumer commentary questions whether Gucci prices are justified
items.summary: Italian-language consumer blog discussion (reflecting ongoing retail chatter) argues Gucci's pricing is 'follemente costoso' (insanely expensive) relative to perceived craftsmanship, echoing wider Italian manufacturer complaints that subcontractors are paid roughly EUR 25 to produce bags retailing near EUR 1,200 — a value-for-money critique that has fed consumer backlash against luxury price hikes.

items.title: Gucci unveils renovated flagship boutique in Dubai's Mall of the Emirates
items.summary: Purely descriptive activation coverage: Gucci reopened a 12,277-sq-ft flagship in the Mall of the Emirates, LEED-certified, with curated art by Lucio Fontana, Gunther Forg, Alighiero Boetti and Richard Prince. Brand-staged retail news with no independent evaluative verdict; treated as activation coverage (sentiment 0) per rubric, included here for Middle East/EU-adjacent regional coverage completeness.

items.title: Luca de Meo discusses creativity and how he's 'reengineering' Kering
items.summary: De Meo interview reiterates plans to renovate over two-thirds of Gucci's store network with simplified product display and secure fine-jewelry areas, while saying creativity 'cannot be planned' and he wants to give designers room to work. Trade-press piece corroborating the structural turnaround narrative following the weak Q3 print.

items.source: Reddit r/handbags / resale community chatter (via secondary resale-guide aggregation)
items.title: 2026 Gucci resale guide flags weaker retention for Michele-era pieces
items.summary: Resale-market guide reports mixed secondhand retention for Gucci: a few icons (Jackie 1961, Horsebit 1955) hold strong resale value, while some Michele-era logo-heavy accessories and eccentric ready-to-wear pieces show weaker per-model retention bands (e.g., roughly 55-70% retention on some bag lines, implying a 30-45% value loss on those specific models) — a soft signal on secondary-market desirability for that design era, not a verified blanket cross-brand depreciation figure.
